submissions.findingTextShort: PMID 17470980 is an agar-phantom cardiac-ablation temperature-monitoring study and contributes zero evidence for glucosamine or osteoarthritis.
submissions.findingTextNormalized: The Glucosamine profile's current sole canonical source, PMID 17470980 / DOI 10.1088/0967-3334/28/5/001, studies esophageal temperature-probe behavior during radiofrequency cardiac ablation using an agar phantom model. It does not study glucosamine, cartilage, joints, osteoarthritis, supplementation, or any glucosamine intervention. This source-to-target edge must therefore be quarantined and must contribute zero weight to Glucosamine efficacy, safety, evidence grade, recommendation, or publication decisions.
submissions.usageContext: Source-identity quarantine only; this is not Glucosamine evidence and must not be reassigned by contextual keyword overlap.
submissions.uncertaintyNote: The defect is source identity rather than a disputed interpretation. Research staging does not itself remove the canonical edge; source-registry and semantic-attestation governance remain authoritative for promotion and repair.

submissions.findingTextShort: A 2026 umbrella review found at most minimal-to-modest knee-OA benefit, with a small VAS-pain signal and possible joint-space effect but no clear functional benefit.
submissions.findingTextNormalized: A 2026 umbrella review synthesized 19 systematic reviews/meta-analyses of randomized trials in adults with knee osteoarthritis. Glucosamine produced a small VAS-pain reduction, while WOMAC pain was not significantly different; WOMAC total and function did not significantly improve. A joint-space-narrowing signal was observed, driven mainly by longer-duration sulfate trials. Significant effects were at or below accepted minimal-clinically-important-difference thresholds, adverse-event rates did not differ from placebo, and most included reviews were rated low or critically low quality. The synthesis therefore supports only minimal-to-modest, outcome-specific evidence rather than a broad joint-support efficacy claim.
submissions.populationContext: Adults with knee osteoarthritis represented across 19 systematic reviews/meta-analyses of randomized trials.
submissions.usageContext: Glucosamine preparations were pooled across reviews, but the structural signal was concentrated in longer-duration sulfate trials; formulation identity must remain explicit before claim promotion.
submissions.uncertaintyNote: Extensive primary-study overlap, generally low review quality, formulation heterogeneity, and effect sizes at or below clinical-importance thresholds limit confidence. Positive pain/structure signals must remain paired with null functional outcomes. Source-registry admission and semantic citation attestation remain required before promotion.

submissions.findingTextShort: A 2024 meta-analysis separated glucosamine sulfate from chondroitin and combination regimens, finding a joint-space-narrowing signal for glucosamine sulfate but no basis for collapsing all products into one effect.
submissions.findingTextNormalized: A 2024 systematic review/meta-analysis included 25 randomized placebo-controlled knee-osteoarthritis trials: nine evaluated glucosamine sulfate, 13 chondroitin sulfate, and three the sulfate combination. Glucosamine sulfate showed a significant reduction in tibiofemoral joint-space narrowing; the glucosamine-plus-chondroitin combination did not significantly reduce pain or improve physical function. The review reported generally good tolerability. These results reinforce that glucosamine sulfate, chondroitin sulfate, and their combination are distinct interventions and that a structural signal cannot be generalized to every glucosamine form or translated automatically into symptomatic benefit.
submissions.populationContext: Adults with knee osteoarthritis across randomized placebo-controlled trials.
submissions.usageContext: Glucosamine sulfate is the relevant intervention for the reported structural signal; glucosamine hydrochloride, other salts, and glucosamine-plus-chondroitin combinations must not inherit the same result automatically.
submissions.uncertaintyNote: Outcome and formulation heterogeneity constrain generalization. A radiographic joint-space signal is not equivalent to clinically meaningful pain or functional improvement. Source-registry admission and semantic citation attestation remain required before promotion.

submissions.findingTextShort: A 2023 meta-analysis found no added knee-pain or physical-function benefit when glucosamine alone or glucosamine plus chondroitin was added to exercise.
submissions.findingTextNormalized: A 2023 systematic review/meta-analysis of six studies involving 297 adults with knee osteoarthritis found that adding glucosamine alone or glucosamine plus chondroitin to an exercise program did not significantly improve WOMAC pain, VAS pain, or physical function compared with exercise alone. This is a co-intervention context rather than a pure supplement-versus-placebo estimate, but it is an important null counterweight to broad claims that glucosamine reliably adds symptomatic benefit on top of established exercise management.
submissions.populationContext: Two hundred ninety-seven adults with knee osteoarthritis across six exercise co-intervention studies.
submissions.usageContext: Glucosamine alone or glucosamine-plus-chondroitin added to exercise; combination and monotherapy arms must remain distinguishable.
submissions.uncertaintyNote: The review pools monotherapy and combination co-intervention contexts and contains only six studies. The null finding does not prove all glucosamine preparations are ineffective, but it must remain visible alongside positive pooled signals. Source-registry admission and semantic citation attestation remain required before promotion.
